content.text: The code reads a request parameter value, stores into map, retrieves it back as `bar`, then uses it directly in `Paths.get(fileName)` with no sanitization. This is a classic OWASP Benchmark path traversal test case, no actual sanitization occurs.

input.justification: The value of 'bar' originates directly from a user-controlled HTTP parameter (request.getParameterValues via the parameter-name matching loop), is stored and retrieved unchanged from a HashMap (no sanitization or validation performed), then concatenated into fileName and passed to Paths.get()/Files.newInputStream(), a path traversal sink. There is no validation, canonicalization, or allow-listing of the value before use, so a user can supply '../' sequences to read arbitrary files. This matches the known OWASP Benchmark path-traversal vulnerable pattern.
